title: 1482-time-varying-forecast-combination-for
universal_lens: The structural unification lies in the nonparametric local-linear projection of a high-dimensional stochastic process onto a smoothly varying weight manifold. By mapping time-rescaled indices to a kernel-weighted least-squares problem, the estimator bridges dynamic factor models and sparse regression under strict mixing conditions.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this primitive maps directly to Bayesian conformal inference by treating the time-varying weights as latent hyperparameters. The group-SCAD penalty acts as a continuous spike-and-slab prior, dynamically pruning redundant predictive features while maintaining valid coverage intervals over rolling out-of-sample windows.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the local-linear estimator with boundary reflection models state-transitions between game weeks. It continuously recalibrates the influence of engine probabilities versus market-implied odds, ensuring that the composite forecast adapts to regime shifts without parametric lag or lookahead bias.

primitives.name: Local-Linear Time-Varying Weight Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Low-dim:** leave-one-out local linear estimator (2)–(4) with Epanechnikov kernel + **data reflection** (Hall–Wehrly/Chen–Hong) at the forecast boundary; reflection cuts asymptotic variance by >70% vs no reflection.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t: discrete time index (dimensionless); T: total sample size (dimensionless); h: bandwidth parameter (dimensionless); \tau: rescaled time t/T (dimensionless); \beta(\tau): true time-varying weight vector (dimensionless); \mu_2, \nu_0: kernel moments (dimensionless); M(\tau), V(\tau): design and variance matrices (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Smooth \beta with continuous 2nd derivative, positive-definite M(\tau), m.d.s. errors, 4+\delta moments.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if M(\tau) becomes ill-conditioned near boundaries without reflection, or if the bandwidth h shrinks too rapidly relative to T, violating the \sqrt{Th} consistency condition.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's rolling window recalibration of situational priors. The boundary reflection exactly mirrors the requirement to combine models for the current week using only past weeks' data.
layer2.telemetry: Average Squared Combined Forecast Error (ASCFE) over out-of-sample periods.

primitives.name: Two-Stage Group SCAD Pruner
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **High-dim:** two-stage — (1) Lasso-penalized local linear (12)–(14) for preliminary weights (estimation-consistent, Prop 3); (2) **group SCAD** (Fan–Li, a=3.7, local-linear approximation; penalty weighted by first-stage norms B̃_j and smoothness D̃_j) (15)–(16), solved by group coordinate descent with Cholesky orthogonalization.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: J: number of candidate forecasts (dimensionless); p_T: dimensionality of feature space (dimensionless); \lambda: tuning parameter (dimensionless); \beta_j: subvector of weights for component j (dimensionless); \|\cdot\|: L2 norm (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Restricted eigenvalues (HD.2), min-signal bound (HD.3), sparsity in the true weight vector across the J components.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when the number of highly correlated redundant forecasts exceeds the effective sample size within the kernel window, causing the restricted eigenvalue condition to collapse.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's dynamic feature selection engine. It prunes dead components each week, acting as a continuous variable selection mechanism for high-dimensional sportsbook and engine inputs.
layer2.telemetry: Selection consistency rate and modified BIC score across Monte Carlo replications.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical derivation hinges on approximating the unknown time-varying weight function \beta(\tau) via a local linear expansion around a rescaled time point \tau. By introducing an Epanechnikov kernel K_h, we minimize a locally weighted sum of squared errors. In low dimensions, standard kernel regression suffers from severe boundary bias; the Hall-Wehrly reflection technique elegantly resolves this by mirroring data points, reducing asymptotic variance by over 70%. When the dimensionality of candidate forecasts J exceeds the local sample size, the Hessian matrix becomes singular. The authors introduce a two-stage regularization: an initial Lasso step provides estimation consistency, followed by a non-concave group SCAD penalty. This second stage induces sparsity at the group level, effectively zeroing out entire redundant forecast streams while preserving the oracle property—the estimator behaves as if the true active set were known in advance. The dualities emerge between the smoothing bandwidth h (controlling temporal adaptivity) and the penalization strength \lambda (controlling spatial sparsity across forecasts). Failure modes manifest primarily at the temporal boundaries if reflection is omitted, or in high-dimensional regimes where the restricted eigenvalue condition fails due to extreme multicollinearity among engine variants, leading to unstable weight oscillations.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits deeply from nonparametric time series analysis, specifically the local polynomial estimators of Fan and Gijbels (1996). The boundary correction traces back to Hall and Wehrly (1986) and Chen and Hong (2011). The high-dimensional extension borrows heavily from the oracle properties of SCAD penalties established by Fan and Li (2001), adapting them to a dynamic, grouped setting. It represents a synthesis of classical econometric forecasting combinations (Bates-Granger) with modern high-dimensional statistical learning.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: In the context of GSE, the 'agents' are the diverse predictive models (e.g., Elo, market-implied, situational engines). Each agent possesses a latent, time-varying competence level. The local-linear estimator acts as a meta-learner that continuously updates its belief about each agent's reliability based on recent performance. The group SCAD pruner embodies a ruthless decision actor that actively discards agents whose predictive signal has degraded below the noise floor, preventing them from polluting the ensemble during regime shifts.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises from cross-layer leakage: if the high-dimensional feature pool includes lagged versions of the same underlying engine, the group SCAD might arbitrarily select one lag over another, inducing instability. Furthermore, if the bandwidth h is tuned purely via in-sample CV without accounting for the serial correlation (\beta-mixing) of the sports outcomes, the resulting weights will be overly optimistic. The anti-collinearity veto requires checking the condition number of the local design matrix M(\tau); if it exceeds a threshold, the local linear update must be suspended in favor of a static fallback.
